title: KV cache compaction: optimize fast path + enforce compaction budgets
author: Samir Qureshi
release_notes: Runtime (flagged): compaction now enforces a per-interval budget and reduces allocator/metadata overhead in the no-compaction fast path; improves tail latency under fragmentation pressure without impacting median latency.
description:
Context: Following the initial compaction engine landing (PR #18457) and scheduler pressure integration (PR #18463), we observed measurable overhead on the “no-op” compaction path (i.e., when compaction is enabled but no move occurs) and occasional thrash when fragmentation crosses the trigger threshold during bursty mixes. This PR optimizes the compaction fast path and adds explicit budget enforcement so we can bound work per interval and protect median latency while still recovering from fragmentation.

What this PR does: (1) Fast-path optimizations: make the common-case compaction tick near-zero by avoiding full block-map scans, reducing lock hold time, and caching the last-known fragmentation estimate; replace per-tick vector allocations with a small fixed scratch arena; avoid unnecessary stream sync calls when no moves are scheduled. (2) Budget enforcement: introduce a compaction budget model that caps compaction work per pool per interval; budgets can be expressed as max_bytes_moved and/or max_us (wall budget for the compaction tick), with a safety cap on max_blocks_per_tick. Budget state resets on a fixed interval boundary and is also decremented on allocation-failure fallback compaction. (3) Observability: emit compaction_budget_exhausted_total, compaction_tick_us, and compaction_bytes_moved counters with pool/region/model_family tags; add structured log fields on budget early-exit to aid p99 attribution.

Implementation notes: Compaction budget is enforced before scheduling any moves and again before issuing copies (to handle partial scheduling). We also ensure budget checks happen outside the allocator global lock; budget counters are per-device (per GPU) but keyed by pool to match routing granularity. The compaction tick now short-circuits early if (a) allocator reports fragmentation ratio below trigger, (b) no candidate segments are present, or (c) budget is exhausted.

Config / flags: Adds runtime flags (behind existing compaction flag): kv_compaction_budget_bytes (default: 0 => disabled), kv_compaction_budget_us (default: 0 => disabled), kv_compaction_max_blocks_per_tick (default: 64), kv_compaction_budget_interval_ms (default: 200). If both bytes and us are set, compaction stops when either limit is hit.

Testing: Unit tests for budget arithmetic + interval reset, integration tests under concurrent prefill/decode to ensure early-exit paths do not change allocator state, and perf microbench to validate fast-path overhead. Ran the bursty-mix fragmentation scenario from benchmark-lab with compaction enabled; budgeted mode reduces compaction-induced p50 regression to noise and improves p99 vs unbudgeted compaction in the worst fragmentation case.

Perf results (local + perf suite sample): - Fast-path compaction tick overhead: ~18–25us => ~2–4us (p50) when no moves scheduled. - Under synthetic fragmentation pressure: budget prevents >3ms compaction bursts; p99 improved 6–11% vs unbudgeted compaction in the bursty-mix scenario (single pool), with no measurable p50 regression.

Rollout plan: Keep default budgets disabled. For canary, enable budgets with conservative values (bytes moved per 200ms) and watch compaction_budget_exhausted_total + tail latency. If we see persistent budget exhaustion with rising allocation failures, increase budget or adjust trigger thresholds in follow-up. This is intended to pair with ENG-2851/ENG-2852 staged rollout.

Checklist: - [x] Metrics and logs added with stable names/tags - [x] Unit tests for budget + fast-path - [x] Perf suite run (bursty mix) - [x] Reviewed scheduler interaction: does not starve decode - [x] Default behavior unchanged (compaction remains off unless enabled; budgets disabled by default)

conversation: Hiro Tanaka (review): The early-exit is great, but I’m worried about calling cudaEventQuery in the tick loop even when no copies are pending. Can we avoid touching the stream entirely unless we actually scheduled moves?

Samir Qureshi (author): Good catch. Updated so we only create/query events when move_plan.size() > 0; otherwise tick returns without stream interaction. Also removed one unconditional stream sync that was left from the initial engine wiring.

Grace Kim (review): Budget enforcement needs to be robust to partial scheduling. Right now it looks like we decrement budget when scheduling moves, but the copy stage can still start a large transfer if the plan was created earlier in the tick. Please add a second guard before issuing copies.

Samir Qureshi (author): Added a second check immediately before each copy submission; we stop issuing copies once either budget is hit. Also adjusted accounting so bytes are decremented on submission (not completion) to keep worst-case bounded.

Sofia Ivanova (review): Can you clarify the scheduler interaction? If budget is exhausted, do we signal pressure back to the scheduler or just stop compaction? We should avoid a case where scheduler keeps admitting and we silently accumulate fragmentation.

Samir Qureshi (author): In this PR we only stop compaction. Scheduler pressure stays based on allocation failures + fragmentation ratio (existing path from #18463). Added a metric + log on budget exhaust so SRE can correlate; we can add a follow-up to incorporate “budget exhausted” into pressure heuristics if needed.

Marcus Reed (review): Please attach numbers for the fast-path overhead and confirm there’s no p50 regression in the bursty-mix suite. Also: can we get a regression test that asserts budget prevents >N blocks per tick?

Samir Qureshi (author): Added perf notes to description and pushed a test that sets max_blocks_per_tick=4 and asserts we never plan >4 moves per tick. Burst-mix sample run attached in CI artifacts; p50 unchanged within noise, p99 improves under fragmentation pressure.

Allison Grant (review): Metric naming: prefer *_total for counters and include pool + region tags. Also add a log field that indicates why compaction exited (low_frag, no_candidates, budget_exhausted).
Samir Qureshi (author): Renamed counter to compaction_budget_exhausted_total and added exit_reason field to the structured log. Tags: pool, region, model_family included.
Omar El-Sayed (review): Looks good. One more nit: fragmentation_estimator caching should be invalidated on eviction. Otherwise we can skip compaction too long after a big churn event.
Samir Qureshi (author): Fixed: estimator cache invalidates on eviction batch completion and on allocation failure paths. Added a unit test covering invalidation.
Omar El-Sayed (approval): Approved. This should make canary much safer; thanks for tightening the worst-case behavior.
Merge (squash): Merged by Connor O'Brien into main as 9f3c2d1 (squash commit message: "KV cache compaction: optimize fast path + enforce compaction budgets").
